title: Follow-up, left knee, stairs still hard

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Good morning, Dana. How has the left knee been since your last visit?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Better on flat ground. Pain is about 4/10 most days, but stairs are still hard going down.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Did you get to do your home exercises this week?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Five of seven days. I skipped the weekend because we traveled.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Thanks for being honest. I measured knee flexion at 112 degrees today, up from 104.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Extension is still short by about 3 degrees.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I can feel it when I straighten all the way at night.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Let's test strength. Quad strength is 4/5 on the left.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any numbness, tingling, or night pain?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No numbness. The swelling is down since last month.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Good. Your goal was to walk the trail with your sister in the fall. Still on track?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I want to be able to walk the whole loop without stopping.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Plan: keep the home program, add step-downs from a low step, and I'll see you in three weeks.

expectedFacts.statement: Home exercises five of seven days
Goal: walk the whole loop without stopping
Add step-downs from a low step
